assessments.reasoning: Section 14.3.1.1 makes omission of the identifier’s initializer an early Syntax Error when the containing lexical declaration satisfies IsConstantDeclaration. The additional bytes from §8.2.3 establish that an ordinary lexical declaration delegates that test to its keyword and that const satisfies it.

challenge.method: Apply the rule to a single identifier, avoiding the independent duplicate-name error, and compare the const and let branches.
challenge.results: Only const satisfies the constant-declaration condition. The rule is attached to LexicalBinding within LexicalDeclaration, which bounds the finding to that grammar and excludes bare for-in and for-of declarations. It imposes no condition on the mutability of an initialized value.

limitations: A bare for-in or for-of declaration uses a distinct production. This early error concerns a binding initializer, independently of mutability of the initialized value.
The rule governs parse-time binding syntax. The mutability of an object later referred to by a const is outside its effect.
